questions.question:
Read the following about balanced budget.

A. The government may spend an amount equal to the revenue it collects. This is known as a balanced budget.

B. If it needs to incur higher expenditure, it will have to raise the amount through taxes in order to keep the budget balanced.

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A balanced budget is a budget in which revenues are equal to expenditures, such that there is no budget deficit or surplus.
 
• This balanced budget is most frequently applied to public sector budgeting.
 
• A surplus budget is if the expected government revenues exceed the estimated government expenditure in a particular financial year.
 
• This means that the government’s earnings from taxes levied are greater than the amount the government spends on public welfare.
 
• A deficit budget if the estimated government expenditure exceeds the expected government revenue in a particular financial year.

questions.question: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2023 amends the Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, __________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2017**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• IGST stands for Integrated Goods and Services Tax.
 
• It is a part of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) mechanism in India.
 
• IGST is levied on inter-state supplies of goods and services, including imports into India.
 
• It is governed by the IGST Act, which is one of the four key legislations under the GST framework.
 
• The tax revenue collected under IGST is shared between the Central and State governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India on 1st July 2017.
 
• It is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that is levied on every value addition.
 
• GST is categorized into three types: CGST (Central Goods and Services Tax), SGST (State Goods and Services Tax), and IGST (Integrated Goods and Services Tax).
 
• The introduction of GST has replaced many indirect taxes previously levied by the Central and State governments.
 
• GST aims to create a single, unified Indian market to make the economy stronger and more efficient.

questions.question: The "Licence Raj" in India during the mid-20th century referred to a system of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Industrial licensing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Licence Raj**

 
 
• A system of strict government control and regulation of the Indian economy from the 1950s to the early 1990s.
 
• Businesses required licenses to operate, leading to bureaucratic delays and inefficiencies.
 
• Aimed to protect domestic industries and ensure equitable development.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Licensing**
 
 
• A specific component of the Licence Raj.
 
• Businesses needed licenses to set up new industries or expand existing ones.
 
• The government controlled production capacity, product mix, and location of industries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trade Unions**

 
 
• Organizations representing the interests of workers.
 
• Negotiate with employers for better wages, working conditions, and job security.
 
• Play a crucial role in labor relations and social justice.
 
 
 
• **Import Restrictions**
 
 
• Government policies limiting the import of goods to protect domestic industries.
 
• High tariffs and quotas were used to discourage imports.
 
• Aimed at reducing foreign exchange outflow and promoting self-sufficiency.
 
 
 
• **Export Incentives**
 
 
• Government policies encouraging exports to earn foreign exchange.
 
• Tax breaks, subsidies, and other incentives were offered to exporters.
 
• Aimed at boosting export competitiveness and improving the country's balance of payments.

questions.question: Article 12 of the Indian Constitution provides for ____________.

options.text: Definition of Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Definition of 'State'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Article 12 defines the state in the following manner

In this part, unless the context otherwise requires, "the State" includes the Government and Parliament of India and the Government and the Legislature of each of the States and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.

The following entities are also included in the concept of "State" under Article 12: Railway Board, Electricity Board, Judiciary, University, State Bank of India (SBI). 

 
• The Supreme Court in the case of Rajasthan Electricity Board v. Mohan Lal laid down the conclusive test for determining the bodies that would come under the ambit of ‘other authorities’.

 
 
• The court held that if an authority has the power to issue directions and any offense against them is punishable by law has the power to make rules that would have statutory effect is an agency or instrumentality of state for carrying out trade or business which otherwise would have been carried out by the state departments, such authorities would come within the purview of ‘other authorities’ and hence would be considered ‘state’.
 
 
 
• In the case of A.R. Antulay v. R.S. Nayak, the Court established that the “State” as per Article 12 of the Indian Constitution will include courts only when they are performing non-judicial functions and not while they are performing their judicial functions.
 
• Therefore, in general case judiciary is not included under the definition of State.
 
• The University of Madras v. Shanta bai AIR 1954 – Supreme Court held that the university formed under Madras Act, falls under the definition of the state. Court laid down the Latin term *EJUSDEM GENERIS* means (of the same kind). It was held that the Preceding government is sovereign, government, and parliament, government, and state legislature and local authorities.
 
• But University as a general does not fall under the definitions of "State". As it will include private universities. And private universities are not state.
 
 
• In Umesh v. V.N. Singh, AIR 1986, the Patna High Court, following the decision of the Supreme Court, has held that the Patna University is "a State".
 
 
 
• The Madras High Court held that SBI is a "State" under Article 12 because it is an instrumentality of the government and has a number of public functions.
